answer:
Treat every parameter gradient as part of one concatenated vector. Compute its global L2 norm, then multiply every gradient by min(1,max_norm/(norm+eps)). Clipping each tensor independently is a different operation. Check finiteness before any mutation and skip absent gradients. With AMP, unscale the complete accumulated gradient before clipping.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** The clipped gradient is $g'=g\min(1,c/(\|g\|_2+\epsilon))$. For an active clipping threshold this preserves direction while bounding the global norm. Under mixed precision, unscale before computing the norm; clipping scaled gradients makes the effective threshold depend on the loss scale and therefore on numerical bookkeeping. [3](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/contents/optimization.html)
